fragment: The Project met its stated objectives.
Efficiency was moderate. Budget execution reached 82% by closure, with delays attributed to procurement bottlenecks in the first two years of implementation.

Sustainability prospects are mixed. Financial sustainability is constrained by continued donor dependence, while institutional capacity has strengthened meaningfully over the Project period, with counterpart staff now able to independently operate and maintain the core systems introduced.

The Project remained highly relevant throughout implementation, aligning closely with national development priorities and the evolving needs of target beneficiaries. Stakeholder consultations conducted at the midterm and endline stages confirmed continued buy-in from government counterparts. However, some early design assumptions about local absorptive capacity proved optimistic, requiring adaptive management responses that, while effective, suggest the original theory of change would have benefited from more rigorous contextual analysis at the design stage.
Impact could not be assessed due to the absence of baseline data and a results framework that did not specify measurable higher-level outcomes.
